strengths: The results in the paper are quite original and significant, to my knowledge, which is a bit limited.
The experiments show that the proposed algorithm works well in practice.
The paper is well written and easy to follow.
Theorems 2 and 3 are novel and the experimental results are convincing.
This paper provides a strong theoretical contribution to a very important topic.
Speculative decoding serves as a refreshing and novel direction for accelerating LLM inference.
This work puts the multi-draft model selection problem on better theoretical footing.
The results seem to be sound from my reading and no obvious errors were found.
The introduction of the two-step scheme are simple and intuitive, making it easy to understand.
The authors provide a solid theoretical analysis for token-level optimal draft selection.
The truncated LP algorithm is novel to the field of speculative decoding and theoretically better than SpecTr.
Extensive experiments, including different datasets, different decoding temperature and different draft models demonstrate the effective of proposed method.
weaknesses: The presentation in Section 4 should be clearer; request to write out the full linear program and then explain the truncation more, including the explicit form of the linear program with all variables and constraints before any truncation is applied, to allow the reader to understand the exact optimization problem being solved.

The explanation of the truncation procedure could also be more detailed; it's not immediately clear how the truncation affects the solution and what the truncated program is actually optimizing, including the relationship between the optimal solution of the full program and the truncated one and potential trade-offs introduced by the truncation.

In the experiment section, please include results for Temperature < 1, which is much more common in practice; evaluate the performance of the proposed method under realistic conditions, such as how the acceptance rate and block efficiency change as the temperature decreases.
In Figure 3, experiments are conducted for draft temperatures > 1.0, but typically target model temperature is set to 1.0 or less; it is unclear how these draft temperatures were chosen.
It would be useful to indicate how the gap between the proposed approach and previous approaches varies as the target model temperature varies from 0.0 to 1.0.

Theorems 2 and 3 provide a nice characterization of acceptance probability, but evaluating the condition seems to require 2^{vocabulary size} computations; a faster way to evaluate these quantities would be helpful.

There are some approximate ways to solve the optimal transport by Sinkhorn methods (e.g., https://amsword.medium.com/a-simple-introduction-on-sinkhorn-distances-d01a4ef4f085); it is unclear if these ideas are applicable here.

The term "canonical architectures" may be ambiguous; it would be good to clarify the distinction between neural architectures and the various drafting methods for speculative decoding early in the paper.
Please expand on what token rate means; is it the number of tokens per second?
The background exposition is insufficient; many key concepts such as the role and form of accepting probability in the speculative decoder were not clearly explained.

The contributions of this work are a little weak; given that speculative decoding shows poor performance with batch size larger than 1, the multi-draft sampling is usually not an appropriate option for speculative decoding, so the authors should emphasize contributions to real‑world speculative decoding applications.
The authors should add a clear notation section with distinct description.

The truncated LP draft selection algorithm involves a sorting operation with O(n\log n) complexity that may affect the final speedup; the authors should report its real‑world time consumption and compare to vanilla multi‑draft selection, especially on models with large vocabularies such as Llama 3.1 (vocab size 128k), and consider the impact of the multi‑stage manner for K > 2 on speedup.

The authors should conduct experiments on more benchmarks (e.g., HumanEval [1], GSM8K [2] and MT-bench [3]) for a fair comparison and report the real‑world speedup to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
